[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended the following agility drills:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Shuttle runs: Set up two cones about 10 yards apart.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. T-Drill: Set up three cones in a "T" shape and run around them.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. 5-10-5 Shuttle: Set up three cones in a straight line with 5 yards between each.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Ladder drills: Use an agility ladder for footwork drills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Box drill: Set up four cones in a square for footwork and change of direction drills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised warming up properly before starting agility drills and mastering movements at a slower pace before increasing speed.  
[USER] User asked for tips to avoid injury while doing agility drills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips to avoid injury:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Warm-up properly with stretching and increasing heart rate.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Wear comfortable and supportive shoes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Focus on proper technique to prevent injuries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Don't overdo it; start slow and gradually increase intensity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Take breaks to allow muscles to recover.  
[USER] User plans to follow the injury prevention tips.  
[USER] User inquired about the frequency of agility drills and whether to take rest days.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended incorporating rest days and suggested aiming for three to five agility workouts per week with at least one rest day in between.
